title: Graph document (cartografo)
description: The format of the graph document: nodes with role/skill/contract, edges with a condition, class metadata (D8) and lineage (D13). This document is the complete snapshot of a graph version — the same content graph_version.snapshot stores in the database (D15) and that comes out as the minimal exportable bundle. Structural validation here is about SHAPE; the four soundness rules (reachable, terminates, edge_with_condition, node_with_contract) are semantic and live in scripts/validate-graph.mjs.

problem_class.description: The identity of the problem class, named by the user (D8). The root of the graph's versioning and the unit the telemetry aggregates by.

nodes.description: The graph's stages. A gate is a node (node_type: gate), not a separate entity.

edges.description: Transitions between nodes, each one labelled by a condition.

initial_node.description: The id of the node every traversal starts from. It has to exist in nodes.

final_nodes.description: The ids of the nodes that close the traversal. Every id has to exist in nodes.

custom_fields.description: The fields THIS problem class declares on the job that crosses the map (t168). The definition lives here and not in the job's schema: `downside`, `upside` and `premise_source` are the vocabulary of asymmetric bets (D14) and would make no sense in software development. Required and possibly empty: a class that asks for no field writes `[]`, and that is what keeps true the invariant that required and properties are the same set — the only optional top-level key is `hooks`, and it is optional because it was born later (t169).

hooks.description: Reactions the graph itself declares: entering a node or blocking on it fires a signed delivery (t169). Optional — absent means no reaction, and that is why every graph written before this field goes on being valid without touching anything, the same non-breaking posture as the node's engine field. They live HERE, and not in a subscription registered from outside through the API, so that the reaction is versioned and proposable like any other part of the graph (D2, D15).

max_consecutive_failures.description: How many failed sessions IN A ROW, on the same job and the same node, block the job (t265). Optional — absent means the default of 3, resolved at dispatch time and never at validation, the same non-breaking posture as `hooks` and `project`: every graph written before this field goes on being valid and goes on dispatching exactly as before. The count is a TAIL count: one session that worked zeroes the run. An engine refusal does not go through here — it is deterministic and stops on the first occurrence, on the runner's side. At the document's root and not per node: a different ceiling per node is another ficha's decision, if the evidence turns up.

project.description: The class's STATIC configuration, published by the input projection at `input.project` (t253). It is what comes from no job and is produced by no node: repository, main branch, test command, conventions, ledger documents. Optional — absent means `{}`, and the projection returns the empty object instead of refusing, so that a graph written before this field goes on being valid and goes on dispatching exactly as before (the same non-breaking posture as `hooks` and the node's `engine`). A deliberately open drawer: the keys inside are the CLASS's, like those of `custom_fields`, and closing them here would demand a schema edit per class. A project-specific value lives in the project's variant (D13); what lives here is what the class declares for itself.

custom_field.description: A field of the job, declared by the class: a name, a type and the node that demands it be filled in.

name.description: The name of the field on the job, snake_case. It is the key inside `trabalho.campos`.

type.description: The declared type of the value. In v1 it is metadata: the stored value is NOT checked against it — the same posture the skill manifest already takes with `budgets`, declared before it is enforced. Three scalars and nothing else, because a ficha field is what a person types, not a nested structure.

required_at.description: The id of the node that demands the field be filled in: the job does not leave that node while it is empty (a deterministic gate, D9). `null` when the field is informative — declared on the ficha, enforced by no node. It is NULL and not absent because the key stays required: the same discipline as the top-level key, and it is what stops 'I forgot to decide' from being confused with 'I decided it does not block'.

description.description: What this field means, in one sentence — what the person reads before filling it in.

node_id.description: A node identifier, unique in the document. Lowercase, digits, hyphen and underscore.

lineage.description: The graph's position in the class's lineage (D13): every class has a base graph and a project may have a variant, which is a fork of the base. The fork is born from a topografo proposal with evidence, never from an a priori decision.

type.description: base: the class's canonical graph. variante: a fork of a base, with its diff and lineage recorded.

base_class.description: The class of the base graph this variant came out of. Required when type = variante.

source_proposal_id.description: The id of the topografo proposal that originated the fork (D13). Optional: a variant imported from an external atlas may have no local proposal of origin.

metadata.description: The document's metadata drawer. Deliberately open to extra keys (additionalProperties: true) while the format has not frozen — the rule of two consumers.

name.description: A readable name for the graph.

description.description: What this map covers, in one or two sentences.

schema_version.description: The version of the document's schema this graph was written against (semver; it matches the version in $id).

source.description: Where this graph came from: the synthesizer, a manual port, an atlas import.

node.description: One stage of the graph. Everything that executes is a skill with a contract; what changes is the role (doing, checking, routing).

role.description: Who does the work, in the domain's own language (architect, developer, tester).

description.description: What this node does, in one sentence.

node_type.description: work: produces an artifact. gate: checks and routes — pass/fail/escalate_human, always with evidence. A gate is a node like any other, and deterministic whenever possible.

engine.description: Which engine executes this node (t141). Optional: absent means the runner's default engine (claude-code), resolved at dispatch time and never at validation — which is why every graph written before this field goes on being valid without touching anything. Free text on purpose, like role and skill_ref.id: what refuses an unknown engine is the runner, with UnknownEngineError, and not a closed enum that would need a schema edit for every new adapter.

model.description: Which model of the engine executes this node (t166). Optional: absent means the engine's own default — no model flag is assembled, and the argv comes out identical to what it was before this field existed. Free text on purpose, for the same reason as engine: a closed enum would force a schema edit for every new model, and what refuses an unknown id is the engine's CLI, at the opening of the session. The catalogue the API publishes is discovery, not validation.

escalation_policy.description: When this node calls for a person (t167). always: it escalates before closing the node, even when it thinks it knows the answer. on_uncertainty: it escalates when it stalls — the behaviour every node always had. never: there is nobody to ask here; stalling is a failure of the node's contract, and the runner blocks the job with a reason instead of opening a request. Optional: absent means on_uncertainty, resolved at dispatch time and never at validation, exactly like engine. A closed enum, unlike engine, because here the three values ARE the vocabulary: a fourth value is not a new adapter, it is a mistake by whoever wrote it.

escalation_recipient.description: Who should be called when this node escalates (t167). Free text with no imposed format, like resposta_padrao and respondido_por: there is no identity system and no role system in this repository to validate against. Stored in the graph and returned by the snapshot; nothing sends anything to it yet — delivering is a future ficha, once roles exist.

skill_ref.description: An opaque pointer to a skill of the registry, pinned by version and hash (D4). The internal format of the skill manifest is another document (t97) — here only the pin matters.

id.description: The identifier of the skill in the registry.

hash.description: A pin by hash of the skill's content (D4): an imported skill is a prompt-injection vector; the hash is what prevents a silent swap underneath a graph that is already validated.

contract.description: The load-bearing piece (README principle 3, D9): input and output as JSON Schema, verification as a list of typed checks. Without a contract the synthesizer composes by hallucination; with a contract, composing a graph turns into matching contracts.

input_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the state projection the node receives (README principle 4: explicit state, never a shared window).

output_schema.description: The JSON Schema of what the node returns to the board.

produces.description: The name of the BUCKET this node's structured output accumulates in, inside the next node's input projection (t253). Absent means a merge at the top of `input`, which is what both factory graphs already did because the field did not exist — and that is why it is optional and breaks no graph. A bucket and not a box per session: two nodes that declare the SAME name write into the same object, and that is how `integrate`'s `merge_commit` lands beside `develop`'s `branch` and survives the `test` gate, which produces no artifact of its own. On a key collision the one that wrote later wins, in the order of the traversal.

checks.description: How what this node produced is checked. At least one; deterministic whenever possible.

deterministic_check.description: A command that passes or fails on its own: running tests, validating a schema, building.

command.description: An executable command, exactly as it runs in the working repository.

agentic_check.description: A check that demands judgement. It verifies with evidence of its own — never with the report of whoever did the work.

instruction.description: What the verifier has to judge, in the form of an answerable question.

required_evidence.description: Always true (D9): an agentic check with no evidence attached is not a verification, it is an opinion.

hook.description: A reaction declared by the graph. A hook does NOT take part in the traversal: it is not an edge, it does not change the current node and it has no way of making the job stop — a hook failure is an incident, never an outcome. The referential validation (node_id exists, id unique in the document) is structural and lives in scripts/validate-graph.mjs and packages/core/src/domain/graph.ts, not in the four soundness rules: a dangling hook is a defect of shape, not a property of the workflow net.

id.description: The hook's identifier, unique in the document. The same character class as a node id, on purpose: they are the two names somebody writes by hand inside this file, and one rule is one rule less to remember.

trigger.description: What fires it. node_entered: a job.transitioned whose to_node_id is this node. node_blocked: a job.blocked with the job stopped on this node. A closed enum, like escalation_policy: a third value is not a new adapter, it is a mistake by whoever wrote it. Nothing fires on arrival at the initial_node — the initial placement is job.created, and not a transition.

node_id.description: The node whose entry or block fires the hook. It has to exist in nodes.

description.description: What this reaction is for, in one sentence.

hook_destination.description: Where the reaction goes. Today only webhook: making the control plane execute a shell command that arrived as graph DATA is another ficha, with a review/permission gate of its own mirroring the skill import gate (D4).

type.description: An enum of a single value today, so that a second variant (local_command) is additive tomorrow, breaking no graph.

url.description: An absolute http: or https: URL that receives the POST. The same rule as POST /v1/webhooks (docs/spec/webhooks-events.md §2).

secret_ref.description: The NAME of the HMAC key, never the key. The value lives in segredo_gancho, in the deployment's database, registered by PUT /v1/hook-secrets/:name and resolved by the control plane at enqueue time — the same instant the url is copied. The document is content-addressed, served whole by the API, written to disk by the export and published in the atlas: a key written here is everybody's key who reads the map. That is why this shape is not merely declared here: since t256 it is ENFORCED on write by scripts/validate-graph.mjs and packages/core/src/domain/graph.ts, which refuse the document with hook_raw_secret when the destination carries a raw secret and with invalid_hook_destination when it carries no secret_ref at all — the same place the hook's referential validation already lived. The same character class as a node id, because the name also crosses a URL path.

edge.description: A transition from one node to another, labelled by the origin node's result.

condition.description: The label of the origin node's result ("aprovado", "retrabalho") when the origin has multiple exits, or the literal "sempre" when it has a single exit. A plain string on purpose: no expression language before two real graphs are pressing on the format.

description.description: When this transition happens, in one sentence.
